item.title: Australia, England set for ODI series opener in Perth
item.description: Perth: Australia and England will renew their historic rivalry when they face off in the opening match of a three-match ODI series at Perth Stadium on Friday. Ahead of the series opener, Australia captain Mitchell Marsh and his England counterpart Harry Brook took part in a pre-series trophy unveiling ceremony in Perth. The two captains also shared a cup of tea at a specially arranged table at the venue, in a light-hearted build-up to the contest. The unique activity celebrated the rich cricketing heritage shared by the two nations, which were among the pioneers of international cricket. The opening ODI, a day-night fixture, will begin at 11.30 am local time. The second match will be played at Adelaide Oval on November 15, before the series concludes at Hobart's Bellerive Oval on November 18. The teams will then switch to the shortest format for a five-match T20I series, beginning at the Melbourne Cricket Ground on November 21. The T20I series will also travel to Gold Coast, Brisbane and Sydney before concluding at Manuka Oval in Canberra on December 2.

item.title: Crystal Palace sack manager Sage after just five months
item.description: Pierre Sage had impressed in France with Lens and Lyon before an ill-fated stint as manager of Premier League club Crystal Palace (Glyn KIRK) Crystal Palace have sacked French manager Pierre Sage after just five months in charge, with the club bottom of the Premier League. Sunday's 3-1 defeat by Liverpool was Palace's fourth in succession in a league campaign in which they have just won two of their opening 10 matches. They also have the worst defensive record in the league, conceding 24 goals so far this season. Palace are 21st in the 36-team Europa League table, with one win from their four matches. "Crystal Palace Football Club can confirm that Pierre Sage has left his role as manager," said a club statement issued Thursday. The statement added three members of Sage's coaching staff -- Jamal Alioui, Damien Della Santa and Sandy Guichard -- had also left Selhurst Park. Palace added: "The club thanks Pierre and his staff for their efforts during their time in South London, and wish them well for the future. "An update on the process of appointing a new manager will be provided in due course." Former Brentford and Tottenham boss Thomas Frank has been tipped to replace Sage in a move that would see the Dane take charge of his third London club. Former Lens and Lyon boss Sage, 47, had the unenviable task of replacing Oliver Glasner -- Palace's most successful manager after guiding the Eagles to their first major trophies in the 2025 FA Cup and the UEFA Conference League last season. The Austrian left at the end of last season, having decided against renewing his contract following a row over Palace's transfer policy, before joining Premier League rivals Nottingham Forest. Sage oversaw Lens's first French Cup triumph last season, while the northern side also finished runners-up behind Paris Saint-Germain in Ligue 1. But it was a very different story at Palace, where his time in charge included a 5-0 thrashing by rivals Brighton in the Premier League. jdg/nf

item.title: Fred Vasseur: Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc “left my room joking together”
item.description: Motorsport photo Ferrari team principal Fred Vasseur has shut down speculation of ongoing friction between Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc , confirming the two drivers resolved their issues during a private sit-down discussion ahead of the São Paulo Grand Prix. The internal dynamic at Ferrari has been under scrutiny following the team's opening-lap clash in Mexico, but the chaotic, rain-soaked race at Interlagos passed without any radio arguments or disputes over position swapping between the two drivers. Speaking to the media post-race, Vasseur confirmed that a preemptive meeting was the catalyst for the smooth operation. "Honestly, we had a good discussion on Friday. We cleared the situation," Vasseur explained. "I think we did a good reset on the mindset, and they left my room joking together." Charles Leclerc, Ferrari, Lewis Hamilton, Ferrari Charles Leclerc, Ferrari, Lewis Hamilton, Ferrari While it remains to be seen if the harmony will hold through the final stretch of the season, Vasseur was visibly relieved by the outcome of the talks. "It's good, and I hope the things will last and stay like this, but we had a good meeting on Thursday," Vasseur added. A "mega lap" deflection The Ferrari boss was in good spirits following the race, even using his trademark dry humour to deflect questions about the intense pressure on the pitwall. When a journalist pressed him on a specific high-stress strategy moment - asking on what lap it occurred and if the cars were still on intermediate tyres - Vasseur completely bypassed the race data. "No, no, no, guys. This is 6:30, it's when I did my sport," Vasseur deadpanned, referring to his morning workout. "And then I made a mega lap. No confusion. The conclusion is that I'm much more stressed when I'm doing sport." To read more Motorsport.com articles visit our website .

item.title: ‘Why can’t we have nice things?’ – Rachel Nichols gives perfect reaction to Steph Curry injury news
item.description: Photo by Kenneth Richmond/Getty Images Stephen Curry is set to miss time after sustaining an injury during the Golden State Warriors’ loss to the Houston Rockets. Curry seemed to sustain a serious abdominal injury halfway through the first quarter of the Warriors’ loss to the Rockets, after getting tangled up with Alperen Sengun. The four-time NBA champion would end up leaving the game and didn’t return, as the Warriors’ medical staff deemed his injury serious enough for him to miss the game. Rachel Nichols devastated by Stephen Curry injury update from Steve Kerr Taking to X following Steve Kerr’s press conference after the Golden State Warriors lose to the Houston Rockets, Rachel Nichols expressed her frustration over his update on Stephen Curry. Kerr admitted that there is a high level of concern surrounding Curry after his injury against the Rockets, but they will have a full prognosis the next day. “D*** IT. Steve Kerr said ‘concern is high’ over Steph Curry, who had to leave the arena in Houston midgame to get an MRI on an abdominal injury. Why can’t we have nice things????” The worst-case scenario could see the Warriors lose Curry for a significant portion of the season, thus leaving them without their best two players going forward. With Jimmy Butler still recovering from his ACL tear earlier this year, the Warriors were more reliant than ever on Curry and his scoring exploits heading into the season. And while rookie Yaxel Lendeborg’s performances have been a huge boost to the team, allowing them to go on a run of winning games, the youngster isn’t ready to be the first scoring option for the team. As for Brandin Podziemski, he isn’t ready yet but will have to settle into the role of the first option for them going forward. So far this season, Curry is averaging 27.8 points, 3.9 assists, and 3.7 rebounds while shooting 50.0% from the field, 45.7% from deep, and 98.7% from beyond the arc. Regardless of how long he is out, the Warriors will feel Curry’s absence in the games he misses. item.title: Police investigation into Vigar's death ongoing
item.description: Billy Vigar died from a "significant brain injury" in September 2025 [Getty Images] The police investigation into the death of former Arsenal academy player Billy Vigar is ongoing, a coroner's court has heard. Vigar died from a "significant brain injury" in September 2025, five days after colliding with a concrete wall surrounding a pitch while playing for Chichester City at Wingate and Finchley's stadium. His parents, Keith and Camilla, told BBC Sport on the one-year anniversary that "the FA could have stopped Billy losing his life because they had so many warnings". Det Supt Colin Chandler, from the Metropolitan Police, told a pre-inquest review hearing that he anticipated he would need another "two to three months" on his investigation. He did not provide details on the lines of enquiry that the police are exploring. BBC Sport has contacted the Met for comment. Vigar's parents were present for the hearing at Barnet Coroner's Court on Thursday, as were representatives from the Football Association and Barnet Council. Former Bath City player Alex Fletcher, who fractured his skull when colliding with concrete barriers next to the club's pitch in 2022, was also present, as was another representative from the PFA. Camilla Vigar told senior coroner Andrew Walker: "I don't understand how the FA waited for Billy to die before they actioned anything when there was so much warning beforehand. "Ben Hiscox dying in 2015. Alex had his big accident in 2022. The investigation they did after that highlighted about 160 high-risk clubs. Wingate was one of them. They did nothing." Keith Vigar spoke during the hearing to raise an "issue with Barnet not being an interested party" in the case. "Personally I don't quite understand how the investigation carried out at the football club, Wingate and Finchley... I see it as a bit of a conflict of interest that Barnet as the local authority carried out that investigation. It feels like they are marking their own homework," he said. A further hearing has been scheduled for 10 February.

item.title: Patrick Mahomes shares what really impressed him after meeting Josh Downs
item.description: Photo by Jamie Squire/Getty Images The Kansas City Chiefs added wide receiver Josh Downs to their roster before the trade deadline in a move that has certainly excited quarterback Patrick Mahomes. Andy Reid was well aware that the Chiefs needed something more on offense after adding Kenneth Walker III during the offseason. The Chiefs had made a bright start to the season, but there were signs of the offense being slightly hamstrung by the options at receiver. As the Indianapolis Colts opened up to teams trading for their players, Downs to the Chiefs became an obvious move for all parties, and the 25-year-old’s arrival in Kansas City has excited Mahomes after the pair met on Wednesday. What impressed Patrick Mahomes about Josh Downs after first meeting It has undoubtedly been a difficult season for Downs so far, with the Colts struggling massively. Daniel Jones was only able to throw one touchdown pass to Downs, but that is expected to change as Mahomes looks to form a strong connection with the WR. “I’m always excited to add another player, someone that’s been productive in this league and that can really help out. From meeting Josh today [Wednesday], really just the mindset that he has, I can tell he’s going to fit in that room perfectly and really help us continue to get better and better as we continue down the stretch here. So I’m excited for that as well,” said Mahomes. “Yeah, I think you can tell just by his intellect and how he’s able to pick stuff up that he’s a professional who knows what he’s doing. He wants to come in, compete, and have success; he wants to win, and so I’m excited for that. “You can also see him interacting with the other receivers in the room. You can tell there is going to be great cohesion there, and that’s the type of guys you want on teams: guys who want to compete and want to win.” Next up for the Chiefs is a road trip to face the Atlanta Falcons at the weekend. Mahomes admitted it has taken no time for Downs to settle in among his teammates at the facility, but how much trust he will have in the receiver by this weekend will remain to be seen. item.title: Lazio Attacker Returns to Group Training, Aims to Return Against Lecce
item.description: Lazio Attacker Returns to Group Training, Aims to Return Against Lecce Lazio forward Albert Gudmundsson has reportedly rejoined his teammates in group training on Thursday morning. The Background The 29-year-old completed a deadline-day move from Fiorentina, joining the Italian capital side on loan with an option to buy at the end of the season. He scored the winner on his Lazio debut, and then had another two cameos against AC Milan and Venezia. Afterwards, he dislocated his shoulder during a UEFA Nations League fixture between Iceland and Estonia, and he’s been one the sidelines ever since. Albert Gudmundsson Back With Lazio Group in Training According to Il Messaggero (via La Lazio Siamo Noi ), Gudmundsson will partially rejoin the group training starting Thursday. Gennaro Gattuso gave his players three days off after Sunday’s draw against Napoli, but work at Formello has now resumed, albeit without the seven players summoned by their national teams. Gudmundsson to Feature Against Mgarr United? The Lazio manager had already revealed his intention to field the Icelandic star during Saturday’s friendly against Matese second-tier club, Mgarr United . It remains to be seen whether the former Genoa attacker will be fit enough to take part in the action. Why Gudmundsson Can Play a Crucial Role for Lazio This is another positive boost for Gattuso, who has recently regained the services of Nicolo Rovella and Adam Marusic. Moreover, Mattia Zaccagni’s condition isn’t as serious as initially feared , so he aims to return to the squad on November 28, when Lazio take on Torino. Probable Italy Lineup vs France: Frattesi to Join Arsenal & Spurs Stars On the other hand, Gudmundsson could be available as early as the Lecce game on November 21. His return would be wonderful news for the Biancocelesti, as he’s one of the few players capable of replacing Zaccagni on the left wing. The versatile Tijjani Noslin started in a wide position in Naples, with Andrea Pinamonti leading the line, but it left Gattuso with limited attacking options off the bench.

item.title: RC Lens reach agreement to re-hire Pierre Sage
item.description: RC Lens reach agreement to re-hire Pierre Sage RC Lens have reached a verbal agreement to re-hire Pierre Sage, according to a report from Foot Mercato. Sage’s exit from Crystal Palace was confirmed on Thursday afternoon. The Frenchman joined the Premier League club from Lens over the summer, having led the latter to a second-place finish in Ligue 1. He is also the man that guided the club to their first-ever Coupe de France trophy. However, his stint in south London was shortlived. He left the club after just 16 games, 10 of which came in the Premier League. At the time of his departure, Crystal Palace were rock-bottom of the table. In his absence, Lens have been in crisis. Dino Toppmoller lasted just six games, and his successor, Yannick Cahuzac, lasted just nine before departing earlier this week (although his exit has yet to be officialised). Sage was the priority target to replace Cahuzac, and Lens may have their man. A verbal agreement between the parties has been reached, it has been announced. GFFN | Luke Entwistle

item.title: Dodger notes: Shohei Ohtani plans, Scott Boras talks Tarik Skubal
item.description: LOS ANGELES, CALIFORNIA - AUGUST 13: Shohei Ohtani #17 and Tarik Skubal #29 of the Los Angeles Dodgers look out from the dugout during a 5-4 loss to the Milwaukee Brewers during the ninth inning at Dodger Stadium on August 13, 2026 in Los Angeles, California. (Photo by Harry How/Getty Images) | Getty Images Dodgers general manager Brandon Gomes talked with reporters Tuesday in Las Vegas, and added more to what the team is thinking as far as signing Tarik Skubal. Jacob Macofsky covered what he talked about in yesterday’s article. Wednesday, Skubal’s agent Scott Boras spoke with reporters and laid out more details about his client that is this year’s biggest free agent on the market. “Much like 2021, there’s a clear intent on a group of players, and we have no reservations by any teams that they’re going to operate within their abilities and freedoms because they want they don’t want to lose to their competitors,” Boras told reporters. “They want the market to be what it is for them, and they’re utilizing their rights to compete. I think they’re very concerned about losing the opportunity to sign select, key players, and they’re pursuing it aggressively.” Maddie Lee of the L.A. Times covers this and more of what Boras said about his highly sought after client, and what the Dodgers pitching staff needs and doesn’t necessarily need heading into the 2027 season (should there be one). Cody Stavenhagen of The Athletic also covers what else Boras is thinking in terms of the offseason and the possible impending lockout, and how in typical Boras fashion the news conference was a spectacle unto itself. The place that Boras’ team had picked to hold his annual press gaggle was not sanctioned by ARIA hotel, and thusly was moved to a different location. According to Stavenhagen, Boras strongly hinted that Skubal would sign before the impending lockout, as did his clients Marcus Semien and Corey Seager in 2021-22 before that season’s lockout. “I think they’re very concerned about losing the opportunity to sign select key players, and they are pursuing it aggressively,” Boras said. One pitcher who will definitely be on the team next season is Shohei Ohtani, but when he will first pitch for the Dodgers is not certain. As Fabian Ardaya of The Athletic discusses , the team is not sure when the two-way player will return to the mound. Brandon Gomes had this to say about Ohtani – “Whatever it is, there’s just a lot of different avenues, and I think for us to unilaterally decide that doesn’t make sense. So it’s really bringing him into the conversation and figuring out how to navigate a full season.” Lots to be decided in the coming weeks and months as the Dodgers look to reclaim the top spot in MLB from the Milwaukee Brewers.

item.title: Gary Player names the one-time major champion who was ‘a better golfer than Jack Nicklaus’
item.description: Photo by Kevin C. Cox/Getty Images Gary Player is never shy to speak his mind and that is what makes him such a captivating person to listen to when he is giving his opinions on the game. Player is one of the greatest golfers ever to have graced our wonderful game, with 159 professional victories to his name worldwide, including nine major championships. Meanwhile, Jack Nicklaus is the greatest of them all, certainly as far as his major win tally is concerned, with a record 18 to his name. Gary Player and Jack Nicklaus enjoyed a great rivalry on the golf course in the 1960s and 1970s, but they were really close friends off it as well. Player got the better of Nicklaus plenty of times during their prime years, but the American obviously had the last laugh, especially in the majors. Despite their close friendship, the South African always gives his honest opinion when asked about Nicklaus as a golfer. Player admires the 18-time major champion more than any other golfer he came up against, but there was one player who was even better than the great man according to the man from South Africa. Gary Player claims Tom Weiskopf was ‘a better golfer than Jack Nicklaus’ Player made an appearance on The Golfer’s Journal and discussed a wide range of topics concerning the professional game. As the conversation turned to Jack Nicklaus, Player claimed that the Golden Bear’s incredible mentality was what made him such an elite golfer. “ Tom Weiskopf was a better golfer than Nicklaus. He really could play. But he won one major because he did not have it! He had the technique but he did not have it (mentality), “ Player said. “ He still did extremely well, but he was not in the category of many majors. He won one major. With his technique he should have won 15. You can see that throughout life. You meet people in business, in marriage and it’s very interesting, to see how that mind works. “ I always tell people that all I hear about today is long-hitting. It’s an asset but it is not a necessity. What is a necessity is a special mind and to be a great putter. Driving, these pros hit eight of them a day, but they hit 29 putts, yet all the emphasis is put on driving. “ Tiger Woods won as a golfer because he was the best putter! “ Weiskopf won 16 PGA Tour titles during his career, including a solitary major championship after he triumphed at The Open in 1973. As Player said, he undoubtedly should have won more majors, such was the quality of his ball-striking. However, Gary Player suggesting that Tom Weiskopf was a better golfer than Jack Nicklaus is surely a huge exaggeration. Of course, Nicklaus arguably had the strongest mentality, but there were not many golfers who were better ball-strikers than him, and there definitely wasn’t anyone who putted better under pressure. Sure, Weiskopf should have won multiple majors, but he never was in the same league as Nicklaus, either mentally or as a golfer.

item.title: Devin McCourty urges Jonathan Taylor to go on strike after remaining with the Colts
item.description: Photo by Kevin Sabitus/Getty Images The Indianapolis Colts were busy in the weeks leading up to the trade deadline, but Jonathan Taylor was not one of the players who got to join a different team. Josh Downs and Keenan Allen both secured moves away from Indianapolis on Tuesday as they joined the Kansas City Chiefs and the San Francisco 49ers, respectively. However, star running back Taylor remains in Indy ahead of what could be a long stretch until the end of the season. The Colts have been nothing short of a disaster this year, having won just two of their nine games this season. Many around the league feel as if Taylor deserves much better than this, which has led to Devin McCourty insisting the 27-year-old must go on strike in the offseason – if needed – to earn himself a trade. Jonathan Taylor advised to go on strike to earn Indianapolis Colts exit The Colts were open to trading away Taylor, but it was apparent that teams were not willing to cough up a first-round pick for the running back. As a result, the 27-year-old remains in Indy while some of his former teammates may now compete for a Super Bowl. “Like, if I’m Jonathan Taylor, I’m trying as much as I can to force my way out of Indy this offseason. Like, I don’t want to be here. I’m not coming to offseason workouts. I’m doing whatever I can because you already told me that you didn’t really want me here. Or not that you didn’t want me here, you were going to turn my value into picks and try to get better for the future,” McCourty said on NBC. “Why do I want to line up and run behind an offensive line when you got rid of our best player? Like, it just doesn’t make sense. Despite playing for one of the worst teams in the NFL, Taylor has still been able to provide a solid return from the running back position. Taylor has racked up 656 rushing yards this season, and eight touchdowns. “I think when you do this as an organisation, and for weeks we’re talking about guys that are going to get traded and you decide to keep them, I just think the message you sent to your team was that not only are we failing on the football field, we failed as a front office to actually trade these guys when we knew we wanted to trade them. We suck at that, too. “Like, I just think it’s bad business as a team for the guys in the locker room. You don’t want to be a part of that. And even if you understand the business, be good at the business. Get rid of these guys. Let’s suck. Let’s let these young guys play. Let’s lose. Let’s get draft picks and then figure it out from there. item.title: ‘Should be suspended’ – Warriors fans demand NBA action over Stephen Curry’s injury
item.description: Photo by Kenneth Richmond/Getty Images It didn’t take long for angry Warriors fans to rewind the tape on Steph Curry’s injury. Golden State’s great start to the season just hit a wall. Steph Curry went down with an oblique injury, and right now, nobody knows how long the Warriors are going to be without him. While the team waits on test results to figure out a timeline, the timing couldn’t be much worse. The Warriors are staring down a tough stretch of games on the schedule, and trying to protect their early momentum without their best player on the floor is going to test the entire roster. Yaxel Lendeborg has stepped up, but not even he could get the Warriors over the line against the Rockets. Warriors fans blame Alperen Sengun for Stephen Curry’s injury Footage of the play between Alperen Sengun and Stephen Curry has been circulating all over social media, and it shows exactly what went wrong. Even though Curry seemed to initiate the tangle with Alperen Sengun, the Rockets center ended up trapping Curry’s arm and turning it upward as they broke apart. You can clearly see Curry wince in pain right after the collision, pointing to the exact moment the oblique injury likely happened. Warriors fans were quick to blame Alperen Sengun for the incident online. This fan started: “Hooks his arm and then yanks it. If someone does that to Sengun, he’s on the floor crying for 19 mins.” “Alperen Sengun should be suspended.” Said another. Another supporter touched on the treatment of Curry: “Look at what Stephen Curry constantly deals with man.” “Sengun needs to be suspended for this.” Another fan added. Lastly, this fan was annoyed: “They genuinely let you get away with anything in the NBA.” Even with all the noise from Warriors fans, the league isn’t going to hand down any punishment here. Looking closely at the replay, it really just comes across as an awkward basketball tangle in the heat of the moment, and Alperen Sengun didn’t seem to have any malicious intent behind it. item.title: “Our Existence Is Political”: Gabby Williams Opens Up About The Politics Of Being A Female Athlete
item.description: Oct 21, 2026; Atlanta, Georgia, USA; Golden State Valkyries forward Gabby Williams (1) arrives at State Farm Arena before game three of the 2026 WNBA Finals against the Atlanta Dream. Mandatory Credit: Brett Davis-Imagn Images Gabby Williams, the 2026 WNBA Finals MVP , thinks that “as a female athlete, just our existence is political.” Williams won the Finals MVP award after the Golden State Valkyries won their first championship. She spoke at the Valkyries’ exit interviews at the team’s Sephora Performance Center practice facility in Oakland. Speaking with CNBC’s Alex Sherman about the WNBA’s place in political and cultural conversations, Williams said , “Being a female athlete just automatically becomes politicized because we’re in a space where maybe we weren’t welcome before.” View this post on Instagram A post shared by Golden State Valkyries (@valkyries) The Valkyries forward said she and many of her fellow athletes understand that playing professional basketball has brought them a larger platform. Discussing athletes’ embrace of their larger platform, Williams said, “I think it’s something that we embrace as athletes.” Williams pointed to players’ past involvement in social and political causes, including the 2020 Georgia Senate runoff and the Black Lives Matter movement. item.title: Joe Mazzulla Explains Why NBA Locker Room Relationships Are More Complicated Than Fans Realize
item.description: Mandatory Credit: Troy Taormina-Imagn Images All the talk in the lead-up to Tuesday’s clash between the Boston Celtics and the Philadelphia 76ers at Xfinity Mobile Arena was about Jayson Tatum and Jaylen Brown’s relationship. Despite being teammates on the Celtics for nine seasons and enjoying success together, Tatum and Brown never appeared to be close friends, and weren’t on the best of terms when their partnership ended this past offseason. While fans at large have obsessed over this lack of relationship, Celtics head coach Joe Mazzulla thinks that is down to a lack of understanding. In his press conference before that Celtics-76ers game, Mazzulla was asked what’s different about NBA locker room relationships that people on the outside don’t understand. “One, I’ll tell you right now, all 30 teams, it’s not Boy Scouts,” Mazzulla said, via Celtics on CLNS. “We’re not all just sitting there getting along, and everyone’s happy-go-lucky. I mean, that’s just not how the world works. So to think that a group of guys are just supposed to just be happy with each other all the time. This isn’t camp. “We’re going after something that’s highly competitive and stressful, and there’s things at stake, and with that comes conflict,” Mazzulla continued. “Doesn’t mean it’s a bad thing. You work through things together. Secondly, you got people that are single, married, divorced, kids, no kids. People have been traded four times. People haven’t been traded at all.” An NBA locker room has players with different upbringings, who have different lifestyles and are at different stages in their careers. They might have great chemistry on the court as teammates, but might not necessarily get along off the court. If you ask the average NBA fan to name the greatest duos of all time, Michael Jordan – Scottie Pippen and Shaquille O’Neal – Kobe Bryant will be common answers. We’ve found out in recent years that Jordan and Pippen didn’t have a great relationship, but they still won six titles together. O’Neal and Bryant had a rough relationship off the court, but still won three championships. In Tatum and Brown’s case, they took the Celtics to the Eastern Conference Finals five times, advanced to the NBA Finals twice, and won a championship in 2024. They might not have been the best of friends, but they were great together on the court. That’s ultimately all that matters. Mazzulla, who led the Celtics to that title in 2024, says that as head coach, you have to bring together all these players with different experiences, but also give them space when needed. item.title: Pierre Sage sacked as Palace manager after less than five months
item.description: FILE PHOTO - Crystal Palace manager Pierre Sage reacts during the English Premier League soccer match between Tottenham Hotspur and Crystal Palace at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium. (is associated with: «Pierre Sage sacked as Palace manager after less than five months») Jordan Pettitt/PA Wire/dpa Crystal Palace have sacked manager Pierre Sage less than five months after his appointment. The former Lens and Lyon boss succeeded Oliver Glasner in June but secured just two Premier League wins and one draw from 10 matches. Palace sit bottom of the table following Sunday’s 3-1 loss at home to Liverpool. Three members of Sage’s coaching staff – Jamal Alioui, Damien Della Santa and Sandy Guichard – have also left the club. “Crystal Palace Football Club can confirm that Pierre Sage has left his role as manager,” read a club statement. “The club would like to place on record its thanks to Pierre and his staff for their efforts during their time in south London, and wish them well for the future.” According to bookmakers, former Tottenham and Brentford boss Thomas Frank is the leading candidate to replace Sage. Palace are bottom of the table after a complete round of fixtures for the first time since December 2017. The Eagles have looked marginally better in other competitions, beating Fulham late last month to book a meeting with Sunderland in the League Cup quarter-finals. Their Europa League campaign has also been a mixed bag, with one win, two draws and one loss leaving them in 21st place after their first four matches. Glasner survived a nine-game Premier League winless run in February. But the Austrian, who joined Nottingham Forest in the summer, had credit in the bank, having led Palace to FA Cup and Conference League glory. Some have suggested Sage – last year’s Ligue 1 manager of the season after guiding Lens to a second-placed finish – was dealt a bad hand, pointing to other areas, including recruitment and injuries, as contributing factors. But even by his own admission, Palace have lacked consistency, conceding more goals – 24 – than any other top-flight club, while scoring 10, leaving them with the worst goal difference in the division.

item.title: Jaron ‘Boots’ Ennis and British star Josh Kelly set for mouthwatering title fight
item.description: Josh Kelly will take on Jaron “Boots” Ennis in a mouthwatering world-title fight, it has been confirmed. On 27 February, Kelly will take on Ennis in Atlanta, Georgia, as the pair unify their super-welterweight belts at State Farm Arena. Britain’s Kelly will enter the bout as IBF champion, while his American foe holds the WBA and WBO titles. The contest surely marks the toughest test of Kelly’s career, as the Sunderland boxer aims to become the first fighter to beat Ennis. Last time out, Ennis stopped Xander Zayas to collect his belts , handing the Puerto Rican his first professional loss. Boots dropped Zayas in rounds one and five, before doing the same in round seven to end the fight. The result also crowned Ennis, 29, a two-weight champion, following his unified-title reign at welterweight. Kelly realised his own world-title dream in January, outpointing Bakhram Murtazaliev to become IBF champion , before retaining the belt with a decision win over Caoimhin Agyarko in July. Both opponents were undefeated before facing Kelly, who will therefore believe he can end Ennis’s own unbeaten run. Kelly, 32, has lost just once as a pro – a stoppage defeat by David Avanesyan in 2021 – and his record also includes a 2019 draw with Ray Robinson. Jaron Ennis dropped Xander Zayas in three separate rounds (Cris Esqueda/Matchroom Boxing) Of Kelly’s 19 wins, nine have come via KO/TKO, while Ennis has 32 KOs from 36 victories. “It’s that time again!” Ennis said in a press release on Wednesday. “I’m adding another belt to the collection. It’s time to look marvelous and put on a beautiful show. 154lbs is MINE! I’m going to keep knocking them down one by one.” Kelly added: “I’ve waited a very long time to prove myself at the highest level – finally I have that moment.” And Matchroom’s Eddie Hearn , who promotes both boxers, said: “What a fantastic unification fight this is. Boots and Josh are both brilliant world champions. This was not a difficult fight to make when you lay out what is there for the winner – three belts around your waist, and just one more to collect to become undisputed at 154 and lay the foundations to a legacy in the sport.”

item.description: PHOENIX — It'll be a two-man race for the 2026 Charles Schwab Cup, and it could be best described as a friendly competition. That's because the two men involved, the only two mathematically alive to win it, are best buds. Stewart Cink, the defending Cup champion with five wins this season, is going mano a mano with Champions tour rookie Zach Johnson, second in points but first in wins with six. Competitors till the end, the two are close off the golf course as well. "He's legitimately one of my best friends in the world," Johnson said of Cink on Tuesday ahead of his practice round at Phoenix Country Club. "I would say the family is as well. The fact that one of us will hold it [the trophy] and the other one, I'm telling you, I'll be the first one to give him a hug if I don't win it." Cink tried to downplay the concept of this being just a two-man competition. "We're playing against a lot more than each other, me and Zach. There's 34 other players that are very capable here in this field," he said. "It's going to be a lot of fun. This is what you really play golf for." They say it's difficult to win, but more difficult to repeat but that's what Cink, the defending Schwab tournament and season-long Schwab points champion, faces this week. "I feel a little bit more pressure because I'm in the reverse scenario from what I was last year. Last year I was Zach," I was like 'win and I win,' but otherwise I wasn't going to win this thing [the points title]. So I was very focused on one thing," Cink said, meaning a year ago he came into this as the No. 2 seed. "As the frontrunner, you feel a little bit more pressure. item.title: Houston is 'very enthusiastic' to get an NHL team but not financing an arena, poll of voters shows
item.description: A new Houston NHL team would be received favorably, according to a new poll of Harris County voters. But the support for financing a new arena is another matter. (Verity Griffin/Getty Images) It remains to be seen if Houston will get a new NHL franchise, but there is no lack of enthusiasm for one among Harris County residents, according to a new poll. However, it's another story when it comes to providing public funding for a new hockey arena. A new study from the University of Houston's Hobby School of Public Affairs released Thursday surveyed 2,750 Harris County voters expected to vote in the recent midterm elections from Oct. 3-8 showed a stark enthusiasm gap between wanting a hockey team and subsidizing a new facility. Pursuit Sports , the company that oversees Houston billionaire Dan Friedkin's sports holdings, is in the process of vetting Houston and Austin for a possible NHL franchise. The process began in late June and the NHL's board of governors could vote on expansion at its December meeting in Florida, with a three-fourths majority needed to pass. A new team is not expected to take the ice until the 2029-30 season at the earliest. Pursuit Sports, which has spent months doing its due diligence in both markets, has not commented publicly save for a statement in June confirming the launch of the vetting process. But if Houston ends up being the choice, it appears Harris County residents seem bullish on supporting a hockey franchise. About two-thirds of those surveyed in the UH poll were "very enthusiastic" (34%) or "somewhat enthusiastic" (32%) when asked about their level of enthusiasm for an NHL team. On the flip side, 18% were "not at all enthusiastic" and 16% "not too enthusiastic" about Houston getting a team after decades of missing out on a franchise . Along gender lines, the results were pretty similar, with 65% of male respondents enthusiastic to 66% of women. On racial/ethnic lines, white voters were at 70% enthusiastic, Latino voters 66% and Black voters 55%. Broken down by age, voters ages 18-34 were 72% enthusiastic, ages 35-54 were at 66% and those 55 and older at 64%. "I was surprised with the demographic consistency on both dimensions," said Mark P. Jones, a senior research fellow at the Hobby School and one of the report's authors. "Harris County voters are very enthusiastic about Houston getting an NHL team, but they're also not at all supportive of Harris County paying for any portion of the new arena. "I think the real key is Harris County voters are enthusiastic about an NHL team but only if they don't have to pay for any part of the arena. If you start asking them to pay for a part of the arena, that enthusiasm is going to drop precipitously." Indeed, the enthusiasm among respondents dipped dramatically when asked what proportion of the cost of a $1.5 billion arena should be funded by Harris County. item.title: Are Yankees on the verge of hiring Aaron Boone’s replacement? | Klapisch
item.description: It’s anyone’s guess how much the Yankees can accomplish before MLB’s lockout begins on Dec. 1, but naming a bench coach to replace Brad Ausmus is expected soon. Given the month-long conversation about the Yankees’ clubhouse culture — or lack of — this decision matters more than ever. Former Astros manager Joe Espada, who was let go in October after Houston flamed out in the Wild Card Series, is the front-runner in the Bronx. Espada was the Yankees’ third-base and infield coach under Joe Girardi from 2015-2017, and he’s maintained a close relationship with general manager Brian Cashman . According to one source familiar with the Yankees’ thinking, Espada’s hiring is inevitable. The source requested anonymity because they were not authorized to speak publicly about the situation. Espada is smart, articulate and well-liked. Espada could also end up being the Yankees’ manager someday. Talk about palace intrigue: It’s impossible to separate the club’s short- and long-term politics. Finding a new right-hand man for Aaron Boone is the immediate goal, but all bets will be off if the Yankees fall short again in 2027. That would be Boone’s 10 th straight season without a championship and would almost certainly mean the end of his run with the Yankees. By hiring Espada now, Cashman would also check that critical second box: a built-in successor to Boone. There are still other candidates out there. Current third-base coach Luis Rojas could be a Plan B, as could Phillies third base coach Carlos Mendoza, who was Boone’s bench coach from 2018-2023 before serving 2 1/2 seasons as the Mets manager. Former Cubs manager David Ross’ name is out there, too. Regardless of whom Cashman chooses, the winner will be fluent in analytics, process-oriented, and as even-keeled as Boone. That’s been the Yankees’ way in the post-Girardi era. I seriously doubt Cashman will deviate from that approach even if the Yankees disappoint in 2027 and Boone is dismissed. That’s why old-school ex-managers like Buck Showalter or John Gibbons would never have a shot with the Yankees. Not even Joe Maddon, the most creative, unorthodox manager in recent history, would get an interview. But that doesn’t mean the Yankees shouldn’t consider a 180-degree turn for the bench coach position. I have no issue with Espada. He’d be a safe choice and a competent wingman for Boone. The problem is that he’s too similar to Boone to bring about the change that’s needed. Cashman made a point this week of saying the Yankees don’t have a clubhouse problem. I’d say yes and no. It’s true that the players get along. There are no wars between cliques. No one undermines Boone behind his back or off the record. Everyone generally pulls in the same direction. item.title: ‘Match Made in Heaven,’ ‘Nobody Can Talk Football Better’ — Aaron Rodgers Has High Praise for Mike Tomlin ‘Absolutely Killing It on TV’
item.description: ‘Match Made in Heaven,’ ‘Nobody Can Talk Football Better’ — Aaron Rodgers Has High Praise for Mike Tomlin ‘Absolutely Killing It on TV’ After a Week 9 bye, quarterback Aaron Rodgers and the Pittsburgh Steelers will face the Cincinnati Bengals in their Week 10 Sunday Night Football matchup. It will be a special night for Rodgers as he reunites with his former coach, Mike Tomlin, on the sidelines. Tomlin will join NBC’s “Football Night in America” crew on-site at Paycor Stadium for the pregame show. Since stepping down as the Steelers’ head coach, Tomlin has transitioned into broadcasting. He is now a central figure in NBC Sports’ pregame, halftime, and postgame coverage. This weekend also marks the first time Tomlin will cover a Steelers game for NBC Sports. Aaron Rodgers Gets Real About Mike Tomlin’s Media Gig As a studio analyst on NBC Sports’ Football Night in America, Tomlin has quickly become a familiar face on Sundays. His wit and on-air analysis have earned praise from media pundits for his smooth transition from coaching to broadcasting. Speaking to reporters on Wednesday, Rodgers admitted that he had watched some of Tomlin’s recent work and was looking forward to seeing him. “I still talk to him. I love Mike T,” Rodgers said on Wednesday. “I have so much appreciation for him bringing me here last year and the amount of fun that we had together and the closeness of the bond that we formed. So it’d be good to see him. I’m not surprised in the least. He is absolutely killing it on TV.” IMPROVE YOUR TEAM: PFN’s Free Fantasy Trade Calculator “The few times I’ve seen him, nobody can talk football better than Mike T. So it is an absolute match made in heaven. Him being on TV and doing what he does. And I don’t know if he still wants to coach at some point, but he’s doing a hell of a job,” he added. Tomlin stepped down as the Steelers’ head coach in January 2026 after 19 seasons without a losing record. Shortly afterward, in April 2026, he accepted an offer from NBC and announced his move into broadcasting. Their matchup against the Bengals kicks off at 8:20 p.m. ET on Sunday, November 15, 2026, at Paycor Stadium in Cincinnati, Ohio. This article originally appeared on Pro Football Network .

item.title: Brewers star Jacob Misiorowski earns historic unanimous Cy Young honor
item.description: Jacob Misiorowski has another major achievement to celebrate after helping the Milwaukee Brewers capture their first World Series title . The 24-year-old flamethrower added the 2026 National League Cy Young Award to his list of accomplishments, earning the honor unanimously when the results were announced Wednesday. The Notorious M.I.Z. Jacob Misiorowski's 2026 NL Cy Young Award is UNANIMOUS pic.twitter.com/4fr6NNcmd2 — MLB (@MLB) November 12, 2026 Milwaukee has now produced four Cy Young Award winners, with Misiorowski becoming the latest to join the exclusive group. Fingers earned the honor in 1981, and Vuckovich followed in 1982. Nearly four decades passed before Burnes restored the Brewers’ presence among the award’s recipients in 2021. Misiorowski has now added another chapter to that history after dominating the National League during the 2026 season. Jacob Misiorowski’s historic season with the Brewers Sep 8, 2026; Milwaukee, Wisconsin, USA; Milwaukee Brewers pitcher Jacob Misiorowski (32) delivers a pitch against the Chicago Cubs in the first inning at American Family Field. Mandatory Credit: Michael McLoone-Imagn Images In his second MLB season, Misiorowski delivered a dominant campaig n, recording 16 wins against five losses across 30 starts. His 1.80 ERA topped every pitcher in the majors, while his 252 strikeouts led both the National and American Leagues. He also finished with a 0.802 WHIP, the lowest mark in baseball. Misiorowski also played a key role in Milwaukee’s championship-clinching victory over the Tampa Bay Rays. In Game 5, he worked 5 2/3 scoreless innings, giving up just two hits while recording two strikeouts. Oct 11, 2026; Milwaukee, Wisconsin, USA; Milwaukee Brewers pitcher Jacob Misiorowski (32) reacts to a call for a balk during the fourth inning against the Los Angeles Dodgers in game one of the NLCS for the 2026 MLB Playoffs at American Family Field. Mandatory Credit: Benny Sieu-Imagn Images Few pitchers can match the raw velocity Misiorowski brings to the mound. He unleashed 1,115 pitches at 100 mph or faster during the 2026 season, but his dominance extends beyond his fastball. At 6-foot-7, the Brewers right-hander also excelled at missing bats, ranking in the 100th percentile for strikeout rate and the 99th percentile for whiff rate last season.
